rounds.text: The stock of Source Industries (India) Ltd [E1] trades at an extraordinarily high P/E ratio of 335x compared to a sector benchmark of 18.49x, indicating that investors are paying significantly more for each rupee of earnings than their peers. This suggests that the market may be undervaluing or misinterpreting the company's financial performance. [E6] Further supporting this view is the P/E ratio of 320.73x against a sector benchmark of 18.49x, which further underscores the disparity in valuation between Source Industries and its competitors. This divergence implies that investors are not only paying an inflated price for earnings but also overlooking potential risks. [E7] The Price-to-book (P/B) ratio at [E2] is 9.10x, significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 1.24x. Given the company's current market capitalization of ₹40.2 Cr and a book value of ₹3.88 per share, this high P/B ratio suggests that investors are valuing the stock based on expectations far beyond its tangible assets. [E4] The absence of any dividend yield [E4] is another indicator of under-appreciation. Typically, companies with strong fundamentals often pay dividends to reward shareholders for their investment. In Source Industries' case, the lack of a dividend suggests that investors are not seeing value in the form of current income streams and may be focusing on future growth potential. This could imply inefficiencies or mismanagement, which are typically underappreciated by investors who focus more on earnings multiples rather than operational efficiency. In summary, Source Industries (India) Ltd appears to be overvalued based on both price-to-earnings and price-to-book ratios compared to its sector peers. The absence of a dividend yield further supports the notion that investors are not seeing value in current income streams but are instead focusing on future growth potential. These factors collectively suggest that Source Industries is being underappreciated by the market, warranting closer scrutiny from an investment perspective.

This does not necessarily indicate under-appreciation but could be seen as reflecting market confidence in the company's asset base and growth potential. However, it is important to note that this metric can be influenced by various factors such as accounting practices or specific industry norms. Without additional context, we cannot conclusively state whether this underpins a bearish view. The stock sits 100% of the way up its 52-week range (4 low to 35 high).
P/E of 320.73x against a sector benchmark of 18.49x.
P/B of 6.07x against a sector benchmark of 1.24x.
ROA of -21.48% against a sector benchmark of 1.97%.
EV/EBITDA of 329.77x against a sector benchmark of 10.05x.
Operating margin is 17% in Mar 2026 against -160% three years earlier (+177 percentage points).
Quarterly operating margin is 6% in Mar 2026 against 64% in the year-ago quarter (-58 percentage points).
A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 4 per share against a market price of Rs 35.3.
That leaves a margin of safety of -704.0%.
A reverse DCF says today's price already implies 48.9% earnings growth, against the 18.0% the base case assumes.
PRICE-LED — Price grew 74% vs profit 25% (5Y) — stock ahead of fundamentals; watch valuation.
